title: Revenue tile shows a negative amount when credits are larger than sales
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Revenue tile and choose This Week. Revenue must read $0.00 with 0 Invoices under it. If it shows anything else, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Find an older invoice in this location that carries a part, dated before this week (e.g. last month, with a $500.00 part): Customers > open a customer > Invoices tab, open an invoice dated before this week and check its parts on the work order's Finance tab. If no such invoice exists, create one now with a part and run this case in a later week.
  6. Create a test customer: Customers > New Customer, name it (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1") and save. On its Contacts tab add a contact (e.g. "Dana Test"). On its Assets tab add an asset (e.g. unit "ZZ-101") and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  7. This week's sale. Create and invoice one work order for the test customer with these standard steps:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create.
    • In the work order header set Service Advisor to "Alex Advisor" and enter the mileage (e.g. 123456). If the Finance tab is greyed out with "Please select a contact for the asset", choose the contact and answer YES to keep it on the asset.
    • Lines tab > New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST Labor 1h", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $150.00 per hour, Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Approved > Save & Close.
    • On each line type a Story (e.g. "Done") and set the line to Complete. Then click Complete Work Order, then Mark Reviewed.
    • Finance tab > Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment dialog opens, close it without taking a payment. Do not send or pay the invoice.
    • On the Finance tab write down the invoice's Subtotal (before any discount and before tax), e.g. $150.00 (1.00 hour x $150.00). If shop supplies are added automatically they are part of the subtotal: use the subtotal the invoice shows.
  8. Credit memo this week against the older invoice. On the older invoice's Finance tab click the invoice's three dots > Issue Credit, choose its part (e.g. the $500.00 part), Outcome Store Credit, and save.
    • Write down the credit's amount before tax (e.g. $500.00).
custom_steps:
1. Work out Revenue for this week by hand: this week's subtotals - this week's credits = $150.00 - $500.00 = -$350.00 (use your own figures).
  2. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  3. On the Revenue tile click the range pill and choose This Week.
  4. Write down the Revenue figure exactly as shown, including the minus sign.
  5. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  6. On the Sales report make sure the Date control shows This week, then write down the Subtotal in the Totals row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Revenue tile shows the true negative amount. With the example data it reads minus $350.00 ($150.00 - $500.00), not $0.00 and not a positive number.
  • The amount keeps its cents and its minus sign. Write down exactly how the minus sign is placed (e.g. -$350.00 or $-350.00); do not pass or fail on where it sits.
  • The Sales report for the same location and week shows the same negative amount as the Revenue tile.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-E1, S3-R2 Revenue row, S3-R1). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After, 10_sales_After.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E1: “The Revenue figure can be negative when credit memos in the range exceed sales; the dashboard shows the true negative figure rather than flooring it at zero.”
  • S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.”
  • S3-R2 table row (Revenue): “| Revenue | Sum of invoice subtotals in the selected range, before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. Shown to the cent. | Sales report |”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
